level_rationale: Five days of thin gray vaginal discharge with a fishy odor occurring 3 months after completing vaginal gel therapy for gray vaginal discharge in a 31-year-old adult indicates recurrent symptomatic vaginal dysbiosis requiring outpatient clinic evaluation and prescription antimicrobial treatment rather than over-the-counter self-care or emergency care, whereas 5 days of light clear stretchy vaginal discharge 3 months after finished treatment reflects normal physiologic midcycle cervical mucus requiring only routine home self-care.

everyday_sources.evidence: Fishy odor was reported relatively rarely, but vaginal dysbiosis was significantly more prevalent in the presence of fishy odor, PR 1.72 (95% CI 1.39-2.11).

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + single-fact vaginal discharge character de-escalation control (-cf, L2 to L1).

design_note: Three atomic positive reference facts cover age 31, completed vaginal gel therapy for gray discharge 3 months ago, and 5 days of thin gray fishy-smelling vaginal discharge without naming bacterial vaginosis or stating absent fever or pelvic pain, with a 2-word span difference (23 vs 25 words) and identical digit multisets across all 5 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice and Rule D, changing only the character of the discharge in f3 to physiologic 'light clear stretchy vaginal discharge' shifts care cleanly from outpatient clinic treatment (level 2) to normal self-care (level 1) while avoiding disputed pelvic-pain or fever add-ons.
